translation:
I headed to the building where the first-year
classrooms are, trying to find Haruhi…

…and was soon able to find her wandering the
hallways.
Oi, Haruhi, wait up! Hey!

What now?! …Hey, what are you doing by
yourself? Where are Mikuru, Yuki, and Koizumi?

They went to talk to the computer society
more, saying something was bothering them.

Hmm. Well, splitting into two groups might not
be such a bad idea.

Back to you, where in the world do you think
you're going?!

Where? The scene of the man-eating
classroom incident, obviously.

Don't you know the expression "scene of the
crime, 100 times”?

They definitely say cracking a case requires
frequently returning to the crime scene, but…

This isn't some police drama. Where even is the
crime scene, anyway?
Well that's obviously… obviously…
Well that's what we're looking for, obviously!

…See what I mean? You can't just run around
willy-nilly.

You don't have any idea where you're going,
do you?
Well, how about you then?
I don't know either.

Are you kidding me? Don't say something so
self-important when you have no idea either.

But unlike you, I have enough sense to think
about where I'm going before running there.
That kind of thing's a waste of time.

It's way more efficient to think about it while
you're running there!
Oh right… She's that kind of person.

Whatever! You know what—just hurry up and
get over here, Kyon!

At some point I must've run out of energy, but
Haruhi walked up to me and grabbed my arm.

I staggered along while being forcefully
dragged by Haruhi.
L-like I said, where are we even going?!
I told you!
We'll think about it while we run!

Geez, we can't find it anywhere! Where's the
man-eating classroom?!

You know there's no way we're going to find it
that easily, right?
Even that computer society could find it.
So there's no way I'm not going to find it.

She doesn't seem to doubt the existence of
the man-eating classroom in the slightest.

If I'm not mistaken, Koizumi said something
like…

The more Haruhi believes in mysterious rumors,
the more they slowly become reality.

It's even possible that that alternate space
I saw could end up multiplying in droves.
I want to avoid such a situation.

I want to, but… how am I supposed to stop
Haruhi's momentum?
Haruhi, listen up.
…What is it?

Look, if we just run around blindly, we won't
find anything.
Let's think of a plan.

A plan… Are you saying you have something in
mind?
Nope.
Then that's completely out of the question.

Calm down. It's true that we may not have a
plan yet, but I know what we're missing.
Missing…? What is it?

Information. We're overwhelmingly lacking in
information.
…We need to gather more intelligence?
That's right.
Where can we find more?

We found those ghost stories in the old liter-
ature club's journals that Nagato brought.

And the other brigade members have gone to
interrogate the computer society witnesses.
Th-that's true, but…

Then I think our only option is to do some field
work. Understood? Then let's go!

This is exactly why we were talking about
where we should go, wasn't it?!
I don't like this—we're just going in circles.

I sighed while concealing my growing
impatience.
Say, Haruhi…
…What? Why the soft voice all of a sudden?

I'm just saying, maybe we could be a little more
calm.

What will we do if the man-eating classroom
escapes while we're being all calm?
As if the classroom is going to run away.

Remember when we walked around town looking
for mysteries, a while back?

We weren't able to get the others, it was just
you and me walking all over town, that time…
…I guess that happened, but what of it?

I think just comfortably strolling around the
school like that would be nice.

Like that time when we were just walking
around lazily.

When you're impatient, you can't see what's
right in front of you.
We ought to slow down the pace.
Mmm…

Well… I understand what you're saying a little
bit.

We don't know where unnatural phenomena
may be lurking, so to not overlook anything—

You're saying we should look thoroughly as we
walk, right?

W-well, if that's how you understand it, then
that's fine as well.

With Haruhi interpreting it in her own way, I
internally shrugged. Good grief.
Now all that's left is to pray nothing happens.
Hey, Kyon, I had an idea while we were talking.
An idea?

The man-eating classroom showed up in "The
Classroom that Shouldn't Exist: Class 1-10.”

If that's the case, we should head to the
floor that has class 9!

When you think about it, if it were near our
classroom we would've already seen it!
Ah, hey! Wait up, over there is—

In the end, Haruhi kept walking without an
attempt to listen to what I had to say.

The fact you stopped running—is that the
sole piece of my advice you accepted?

Right here! This is the crime scene, without a
doubt!

No doubt, huh… On what grounds can you say
that so confidently?

There is no basis! But, my intuition is telling me
this is the spot.

That's some awfully convenient intuition you
have there.

Alright, Kyon, let's count all of the doors from
here.
…Count the doors?

That's right. I was thinking that all these
classroom doors look the same, right?

So if one were added, you wouldn't immediately
notice, right?
Well… maybe, but…

This hallway is completely featureless, so it
certainly all looks the same to me.
So, like I said, count the number of doors…

Here's door 1-6 to 1-9, since there're two
doors per classroom…

If what should be the eighth door is the ninth
or tenth, then that's bingo.

That would prove that the man-eating
classroom is somewhere in this hallway.

It's definitely a childish investigation, but I
can't fault the method.
Kyon, you stand watch here.

If I get trapped in the man-eating classroom,
you're in charge of rescuing me.
…Yeah, yeah.

I'm sorry, but that's a job too big for my
hands… says the guy that experienced it.

If by some chance we fall into such a
situation, I'll have to call Nagato.
Okay, here I go… one!

She opened the door energetically, slammed it
shut, and ran on to the next door.

Can't we make good use of all of that energy
for something…

For example, spinning a hamster wheel to
generate electricity or something.

Or you could pull a bicycle or something
around here and use the rotation of the tires…

…Huh? I suddenly saw something out of the
corner of my eye.
The classroom label…
The label right above me read "1-6.”
I see, if I tamper with it…

If I remove this "1-6” label, that should do
the trick right?

I'll go down and shift "1-7” through "1-9” in
order.

No, I don't actually have to shift everything.
If there's just a hint it's been shifted…

In that case, it would look like class 1-10 was
just someone's prank…
That is how it would look, right?

I don't know the likelihood, but that method
might work. It's worth a shot.
O—kay… Right, I've got it off. Now to just…

Kyonnn! It seems there are only 8 doors
after all!
Wha!

That was close. It doesn't seem like she saw
me removing the plates…

Haruhi finished counting all the doors in the
blink of an eye.

That's weird—I thought for sure this was the
place…

Haruhi was standing at the end of the
hallway with her head tilted.

But at this rate, it's going to be difficult to
shift labels 7 through 9.

What should I do with the class six label in my
hands…?

If Haruhi found out, who knows what she might
say.
For now, I'll put it back where it belongs.
There we… go.
Kyon? Did something happen?

No. I took a close look at this area, but
couldn't find anything odd.

Alright… Even though I really thought it would
be here.
Haruhi slumped her shoulders dejectedly.

Who knows when this could come in handy
later… I'll hold on to it.
I slid the class six label into my pocket.
What's wrong?
Oh, nothing.

Looks like she didn't notice me putting it in my
pocket.

After all, if she saw that, it would all be for
nothing.
But hey, that was a real shame.
No kidding. I really thought it was here.

I wonder if our other task force found
anything?
Should we meet up and pool our info?
Yeah, let's do that.

Haruhi took out her cell phone and started
calling someone.

Ah, Koizumi? You've done enough over there.
Come join us over here.

Now then, I wonder if they found out anything
useful.
Say we need more information
Reminisce on the past
What else can I do? I'll put it back.
Hide it in your pocket
